title: Maximum balanced nonlinearity in eight variables
summary: The maximum nonlinearity of a balanced Boolean function on eight variables is 116; in particular, the spectral target 118 is impossible.

formal_statement.body: For every $f:\mathbb F_2^8\to\mathbb F_2$ with $|f^{-1}(1)|=128$, prove $\operatorname{NL}(f)\le 116$, and construct a balanced function for which equality holds.

scope.domain: Balanced Boolean functions and Walsh spectra
assumptions: Nonlinearity is distance from the first-order Reed--Muller code
scope.unresolved_remainder: Any claim beyond the eight-variable balanced case is outside this record.

citations.label: Picek et al. balanced Boolean-function search targets

progress.summary: Earlier balanced-function constructions and bounds left the eight-variable target as a finite extremal question.
A balanced eight-variable search target was recorded in the subsequent computational literature.
citation_labels: Picek et al. balanced Boolean-function search targets

progress.summary: Lean proves the sharp maximum 116 through complete local enumeration, 69 integer Farkas certificate replays, 13 terminal profile exclusions, and an explicit equality witness.

lean.trusted_base: Lean 4.29.1, mathlib, and the native_decide compiled evaluator for fixed finite enumeration, certificate, parity, normalization, and witness checks; no user-declared axioms
